data.title: India EM weight rises 4 pp: Axis lists 3 factors that can sustain FII flows
data.description:
Clocking a sharp trend reversal in foreign institutional investor (FII) positioning, Indian equities attracted nearly $16 billion in foreign equity inflows since mid-October, with artificial intelligence (AI) trade unwinding emerging as the immediate catalyst.
 
This, along with sharp outperformance by India vis-à-vis peers, boosted its weight in the emerging market (EM) benchmark index by 4 pp since October 1 to 14.7 per cent, according to an analysis by Axis Mutual Fund.
 

What gives India an edge?

Given India's diversification - a domestic-demand-led earnings base and lower direct exposure to the AI theme - FIIs returned dramatically to the Indian stock market. Analysts believe that India will continue to remain a safe-haven as AI unwinding continues globally.
 
 
"This FPI buying appears to be a structural shift away from AI and AI-related stocks to India’s diversified market. The trend of FII buying is likely to continue in the near-term," opined Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. 
ALSO READ: 'Remain constructive on Indian equities irrespective of how global markets do'
 
Axis Capital also identified three triggers that positions India in an advantageous position.
 
- Sector mix: India's benchmarks are skewed towards financial services, consumption, industrials and domestic services than in the hardware suppliers at the centre of the AI selloff.
 
- Positioning: FIIs were net sellers in Indian stock markets for two years, selling stocks worth $60 billion. Benchmark rebalancing is now expected to cut net short position on India, which can generate significant buying pressure.
 
- Oil cools down: Any sustained easing in crude prices bodes well for India’s external balance, inflation outlook and corporate margins, which further supports foreign investor buying.
 
AI unwinding with three shocks: investors were no longer simply extrapolating AI demand, but questioning the durability of profits and the returns on an increasingly capital-intensive build-out; second shock was political as Democrats won a decisive victory in the midterms, bringing data-centre electricity costs, water consumption and local permitting into sharper political focus. The result was greater uncertainty over project timelines, grid connections and regulatory approvals. And the final nail was the Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia.
 
In the medium term, Axis Capital believes AI infrastructure spending is set to moderate vs. previous projections as "rising financing costs, regulatory uncertainty and doubts over investment returns force a reassessment of capacity plans".
 
India, it therefore sad, may continue to benefit from diversification away from crowded AI exposures for the next few weeks, although a disorderly global selloff could eventually overwhelm its relative advantage (unlikely for now).
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: How Zaheer Khan-backed Anchor Sports builds cricket's business in Europe
data.description:
Over six months of rapid expansion, Stockholm-based Anchor Sports AB, co-owned by former India fast bowler Zaheer Khan, has built a three-continent cricket portfolio spanning Belgium, Sri Lanka and Canada. Its stiffest commercial test, however, sits in continental Europe, where the group is absorbing early losses to prove franchise T20 cricket can sustain itself without relying on gambling sponsors.
 
Anchor's push comes amid a fresh wave of Indian capital entering European cricket ahead of the sport's return to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. While the higher-profile European T20 Premier League (ETPL), co-founded by actor Abhishek Bachchan across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands with former India captain Rahul Dravid among its team owners, wrapped up its inaugural season in September, Anchor is backing a slower, grassroots-led model on the mainland.
 
 
Its flagship European side, the Antwerp Anchors, finished runners-up in Belgium's inaugural International Cricket Council (ICC)-approved EUT20 Belgium league in June. The franchise has brought State Bank of India (SBI) and Coca-Cola on board as early sponsors, though its owners declined to disclose revenue, expenditure or a timetable for breaking even.
 
Seeded with profits from founder Nagendra Siddoutam's Stockholm-headquartered IT services firm Acumant, a 200-person Microsoft and artificial intelligence consultancy that acquired local technology firm Northprim in December 2025, Anchor remains firmly in investment mode. "At this point there's a lot of burn, but eventually we'll get to profits," Siddoutam told Business Standard, comparing the venture to the IT product company he set up after Acumant. While IT services can generate profits from day one, building a sports property requires upfront capital before earning a return, he said. 
Mr. Nagendra Siddoutam, Founder, Anchor Sports
 
No IPL copy-paste
 
Khan's route into franchise ownership began through a Mumbai padel partner who introduced him to Siddoutam, and firmed up once he learnt that chief executive Faisal Shariff was running the venture. "Faisal and I go back 25 years," Zaheer Khan said, noting that Shariff started out at Rediff around the time Khan began his international career. He wanted to work with people he trusted on a project built to outlast a single tournament.
 
Both Khan and Shariff are wary of importing India's franchise blueprint to Europe. "You can't just copy it as a tournament," Khan said of the Indian Premier League (IPL).
 
Where the IPL could draw on India's economic scale and vast broadcast audience, European leagues must first raise the standard of cricket available to local players, Khan argued. In Belgium, EUT20 rules paired domestic Belgian cricketers with international names such as Martin Guptill, Moeen Ali and David Wiese.
 
Khan credits South Asian diaspora communities for much of Europe's early participation, but expects better facilities, stronger opponents and the Olympic spotlight to broaden the playing base. That thinking also underpins Anchor's proposed mixed-gender T20 competition, Project EQUAL, aimed at drawing new audiences in Germany and wider Europe. "A lot of the stars of women's cricket today grew up playing cricket with the boys, didn't they?" Khan said, adding that the competition is designed to give that informal pathway an organised structure.
 
Shariff, who served as the IPL's first digital director under Lalit Modi, cautioned against chasing short-term spectacle, a real risk in Europe where earlier ambitions such as the Euro T20 Slam collapsed after repeated postponements. "You don't want to start with a bang and end quickly, before you even get a couple of seasons in and the franchise and the broadcaster start making some profits," he said. 
Mr. Faisal Shariff, CEO, Anchor Sports
 
From Stockholm schools to three continents
 
Anchor's franchise network grew out of grassroots work in Sweden, where Siddoutam has lived for more than 16 years and still plays club cricket. Seeing promising players held back by weak infrastructure, the group built an indoor facility in Stockholm, began working with local schools and brought in former India coach Gary Kirsten and former wicketkeeper Kiran More for youth camps.
 
When plans for an under-23 league in Sweden fell through, Anchor pivoted to Belgium's newly announced league, organised by Destino Legends Sports LLC and the Belgian Cricket Federation. In June, it also signed a youth-development partnership with Denmark's governing body, Dansk Cricket-Forbund.
 
Expansion accelerated in the second half of 2026. In August, Anchor acquired four-time Lanka Premier League (LPL) champions Jaffna, rebranding the side Anchor Jaffna Kings as it finished runners-up in the 2026 final. A month later, Khan joined the ownership group of Anchor's men's and women's Vancouver Anchors franchises in Canada's Super 60 league, reuniting with former India teammate Yuvraj Singh, a stakeholder in the competition.
 
The diaspora bridge and the betting risk
 
Commercially, Anchor's pitch shifts by market. In Test-playing Sri Lanka, cricket needed little introduction. In Antwerp and Vancouver, diaspora demographics offered the starting point. "You go to Antwerp, you feel like you're in Gujarat, to be honest. You go to Vancouver, you feel like you're in Punjab," Siddoutam said.
 
That community footprint helped bring SBI on board in Antwerp. Coca-Cola, announced as an official Antwerp Anchors sponsor in June, required a different approach because its Belgian business knew little about cricket.
 
"Over the next five to six years, Siddoutam wants local European companies and multinationals with sizeable operations in India, such as Sweden's Ericsson and IKEA, to anchor sponsorship revenue. Just as crucially, he wants betting sponsorships kept to a minimum, warning that young leagues risk distorting their finances by chasing quick gambling cash before building a local market.
 
That caution tracks a sharper regulatory squeeze across global sport. According to an October 2026 preview of SportBusiness's Global Betting Report, gambling and gaming firms continue to pour billions into sports sponsorship and advertising worldwide, backing major European properties including Italy's Serie A and Germany's Bundesliga, even as governments and governing bodies curb their visibility.
 
English Premier League clubs have given up front-of-shirt gambling sponsorships, Italy has imposed a sponsorship ban that operators have sought to sidestep through 'infotainment' brands, and Australia has legislated a phase-out running to 2031. In the starkest warning yet for sports properties dependent on gambling money, Brazil banned fixed-odds betting and its advertising outright on September 25, 2026, abruptly halting one of the fastest sponsorship booms in global sport.
 
Indian cricket felt a similar jolt closer to home after the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 prompted Dream11 to exit as the national team's lead sponsor. For a challenger property like Anchor, walking away from easy betting money makes the early burn harder to absorb. Whether local European brands fill that gap will decide if its long game pays off.

data.title: Layoffs and AI fears: 72% of India's tech workers want to switch careers
data.description:
India's technology sector, long regarded as one of the country's most attractive career destinations for its high salaries and global opportunities, is facing a growing crisis of confidence among its own workforce. As layoffs, restructuring and concerns about artificial intelligence reshape the industry, nearly three out of four technology professionals in India say they would switch to an entirely different career if given the opportunity.
 
A survey of 2,958 India-based professionals by anonymous workplace community platform Blind found that 72% would leave their current careers for a completely different profession if there were no financial costs or retraining requirements. 
72% said they would switch to a completely different career tomorrow if it required no cost or retraining. The largest group, 42%, would make the move as long as the pay stayed the same. Only 13% said they are happy where they are.
 
 
While 30% said they would make the switch immediately, another 42% said they would do so if they could retain their existing salaries. Only 13% said they were happy with their current careers and would not consider leaving.
 
The findings point to a growing disconnect between the financial rewards associated with technology jobs and professionals' long-term satisfaction and confidence in the sector.
 
The reluctance to remain in technology is also extending to the next generation. Around 56% of respondents said they would probably or definitely not encourage their children to pursue careers in tech. Nearly one in three, or 31%, said they would definitely discourage them.
 
" The urge to leave was strongest at Intuit (89%), Goldman Sachs (87%), PayPal (87%), Visa (86%), Expedia Group (83%). It ran nearly as high at Oracle (79%), which has reportedly cut about 12,000 jobs in India this year, as well as at Salesforce (79%) and Adobe (78%), where Blind users have reported silent layoffs in India. Even at Meta and Apple, where it was lowest, more than half would switch," the company said in a statement. 
 
The career shift has already shown up on Blind. With more than a month left in the year, posts written in India about leaving software engineering are up 37.5% from all of 2025. For a growing number of India's tech workers, the question is no longer which company to join next, but whether to stay in tech at all.
 
"They don’t want the next generation pursuing tech, either. 56% said they would definitely or probably not encourage their child to go into tech. Nearly 1 in 3 said definitely not. That view holds even at the companies young Indians most want to join. At Microsoft, the largest group of respondents, 67% would steer their child away from tech, and over 50% felt the same at Google and Amazon," said Blind in a release.
 
The survey comes amid continued restructuring across the technology industry, with concerns over job security, changing skill requirements and the impact of artificial intelligence influencing career decisions. 
Blind surveyed 2,958 India-based professionals between November 6 and 19, 2026. Company figures include only companies with at least 10 responses to the question.
 
Healthcare beats software engineering as preferred career choice
 
When asked which profession they would recommend to a young person starting out today, respondents showed a clear preference for careers they believe offer greater long-term stability or are less vulnerable to automation.
 
Medical and healthcare careers emerged as the most preferred option, selected by 34% of respondents.
 
Artificial intelligence and machine learning came second, with 19%, followed by government and public sector jobs at 15%.
 
Other technology roles, including data, cybersecurity and hardware, accounted for 10% of responses. Law and finance also received 10%, while arts and teaching were chosen by 8%.
 
Software engineering ranked last, with just 4% of respondents recommending it as a career choice.
 
Notably, not a single respondent from Google, Meta or NVIDIA selected software engineering as their preferred career recommendation for young people.
 
The preference for healthcare and public sector careers suggests that professionals are increasingly weighing factors beyond salary, including job security, resilience to technological disruption and long-term earning potential.
 
AI creates a career paradox
 
The survey also highlights an interesting contradiction in how technology workers view artificial intelligence.
 
While software engineering received only 4% of recommendations, AI and machine learning emerged as the second-most preferred career path, attracting 19% of responses.
 
This suggests that professionals are not necessarily turning away from technology altogether. Instead, they may be reassessing which technology skills and roles will remain valuable as AI adoption accelerates.
 
The preference for healthcare, government employment and specialised technology functions also reflects a growing interest in careers perceived to offer more durable opportunities.
 
Asked which path they would most recommend to someone starting out today, respondents leaned toward work AI cannot easily replace, or into AI itself. Medicine and healthcare led at 34%, and 15% picked government or public sector jobs. AI and machine learning came second at 19%. In a Blind thread on which profession has the highest earning potential over a lifetime in India, an Apple employee replied: "IAS (civil services) followed by IPS. Earn more than politicians, never get voted out." In another thread, a Cisco employee listed hands-on jobs: "Landscaper. Plumber. Hvac technician. Dentist. Veterinarian. Physical therapist. Nurse."
 
The findings come at a time when businesses are increasingly integrating AI into software development and other functions, raising questions about the future demand for traditional technology roles.
 
However, the survey does not establish that AI has directly caused professionals to consider leaving the industry. Job insecurity, workplace satisfaction, compensation and changing career expectations could also influence these responses.
 
The Blind survey was conducted between November 6 and November 19, 2026, among 2,958 India-based professionals. Company-level figures include only employers with at least 10 responses to the relevant question.
 
Separately, Blind used its AI tool Clair to analyse discussions posted between January 1, 2025, and November 17, 2026, about leaving technology or software engineering for a different career.

data.title: India to see 1.38 cr white-collar jobs in 2027 as hiring growth hits 8.16%
data.description:
India's white-collar job market is expected to gather pace in 2027, with hiring projected to grow 8.16% and the number of jobs forecast to reach 1.38 crore, according to the latest foundit Insights Tracker.The projected growth marks a significant acceleration from the 3.30% year-on-year increase recorded in 2026.
 
Growth was led by Non-profit Organisations (+19.44%), Real Estate (+16.09%) and Travel & Tourism (+13.76%), while IT roles recorded the strongest occupational growth at 20.28%. Hyderabad (+8.51%) and Bengaluru (+6.71%) emerged as the leading hiring markets. 
Non-profits stay on top as Real Estate climbs to second
 
2027 outlook: 1.38 crore jobs projected
 
India’s white-collar hiring market is forecast to grow 8.16% in 2027, compared with 3.30% in 2026, with 1.38 crore jobs projected for the year. Growth is expected to be driven by Consumer Electronics, Retail, Manufacturing and recovering demand in BFSI and Logistics & Transportation, alongside continued opportunities for technology professionals and mid-career talent.
 
 
Companies are likely to place greater emphasis on productivity, operational efficiency and business outcomes, with related hiring projected to increase by 15-20%. At the same time, mid-career professionals, particularly those with 7–10 years of experience, are expected to remain an important talent segment, accounting for 21% of overall hiring demand.
 
Demand for specialised capabilities in areas such as risk, compliance and cybersecurity is also expected to rise by 12%. Alongside external hiring, organisations are likely to place greater focus on reskilling and internal talent mobility, with these initiatives potentially accounting for 20-30% of positions filled.
 
“2026 has been a year of measured hiring. Employers expanded their teams thoughtfully and placed a premium on experienced professionals. Sectors like real estate, travel and healthcare added momentum, even as BFSI and IT services remained cautious. The strong demand for tech roles outside the IT sector shows how widely these skills are now needed. As hiring picks up in 2027, we expect growth to extend to more cities, more sectors and to early-career professionals, who are set to see stronger opportunities,” said Tarun Sinha, CEO, foundit.
 
Industry hiring remains uneven; Consumer Electronics and Retail set to lead in 2027
 
Non-profit Organisations recorded the strongest hiring growth in 2026 at 19.44%, followed by Real Estate (+16.09%), Travel & Tourism (+13.76%) and Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals (+12.34%). Meanwhile, BFSI (-5.00%) and Logistics & Transportation (-2.52%) recorded declines.
 
The 2027 outlook points to stronger demand in Consumer Electronics (+14.25%), Retail (+13.99%) and Manufacturing (+12.02%). BFSI (+10.03%) and Logistics & Transportation (+10.15%) are also projected to return to positive growth. 
Coimbatore is projected to lead hiring growth in 2027 at 12.52%, reversing its 1.86% decline in 2026, followed by Bengaluru (+11.29%) and Hyderabad (+10.33%).
 
IT roles lead occupational growth at 20.28%
 
IT recorded the strongest occupational growth at 20.28% in 2026, followed by Senior Management (+8.11%) and Marketing & Communications (+7.21%). Notably, IT occupations grew despite a 1.66% decline in the IT - Software & Services industry.
 
For 2027, IT (+10.30%), HR & Admin (+8.93%) and Senior Management (+8.56%) are projected to lead occupational hiring growth.
 
Hyderabad leads hiring in 2026; Coimbatore projected to top growth in 2027
 
Hyderabad (+8.51%) led city-wise hiring growth in 2026, followed by Bengaluru (+6.71%), Mumbai (+6.15%) and Kochi (+5.57%). In contrast, Kolkata (-10.03%) and Chandigarh (-11.19%) recorded declines.
 
Coimbatore is projected to lead hiring growth in 2027 at 12.52%, reversing its 1.86% decline in 2026, followed by Bengaluru (+11.29%) and Hyderabad (+10.33%).
 
Mid-career professionals see strongest hiring demand
 
Professionals with 7–10 years of experience recorded the highest hiring growth in 2026 at 8.63%, followed by those with 11–15 years (+5.54%). Entry-level hiring remained subdued at 0.69%, while demand for professionals with 4–6 years of experience declined 0.35%.
 
The outlook for 2027 indicates continued demand for mid-career talent (+7.51%), alongside improving opportunities for professionals with 0–3 years of experience (+4.64%). 
IT Jobs Grew 20% Even as Software Industry Hiring Slowed: What the Data Shows
 
Key points to note: 
The IT paradox: IT occupations grew 20.28%, even as the IT software and services industry declined 1.66%. This is arguably the most interesting finding.
 
The fresher recovery: Entry-level hiring is forecast to grow 4.64%, although mid-career professionals remain the strongest segment.
 
The Coimbatore surprise: Hiring is projected to rise 12.52% after declining 1.86% in 2026.
 
The sector reversal: BFSI is expected to move from a 5% contraction to 10.03% growth, while travel and tourism could reverse from 13.76% growth to a 3.67% decline. 
The outlook for 2027 indicates continued demand for mid-career talent (+7.51%), alongside improving opportunities for professionals with 0–3 years of experience (+4.64%).

data.title: Gold Spot comeback: How the orange drink became a hit, then disappeared
data.description:
Coca-Cola is reportedly preparing to bring back Gold Spot, its orange-flavoured fizzy drink, after a 26-year hiatus. According to a report in The Economic Times, Gold Spot, which was acquired by Coca-Cola from the Parle group in 1993, is expected to return in a low-sugar or no-sugar formulation as the beverage maker looks to tap changing consumer preferences and counter intensifying competition.
 
The reported revival also found an unlikely social media moment over the weekend when photographs of former Indian cricket team captain MS Dhoni and his wife, Sakshi, with Gold Spot cans went viral on social media. However, it remains unclear whether Dhoni has been signed to endorse the brand.
 
 
Gold Spot, known for its taglines 'Zing Thing' and 'Livva Little Hot, Sippa Gold Spot', was discontinued by Coca-Cola in 2000 to make way for its global orange drink Fanta.
 
From Parle's stable to Coca-Cola
 
Gold Spot was launched by Parle in 1952, when India's packaged soft drink market was still taking shape. Its orange flavour and distinctive positioning made it one of the country's familiar home-grown fizzy drinks. Its advertising tagline, 'Zing Thing', was an instant hit among the youth.
 
Parle's beverage portfolio grew over the years to include Limca, launched in 1971, Maaza in 1974 and Thums Up in 1978. These brands gained ground after Coca-Cola exited India in 1977, following disagreements with the government over foreign ownership rules and requirements to disclose proprietary information.
 
Parle sold Gold Spot to Coca-Cola when the latter returned to India in 1993. Coca-Cola also acquired Parle's other beverage brands, including Thums Up, Limca, Maaza, Rim Zim and Citra. The deal also gave Coca-Cola a ready-made portfolio of Indian drinks with considerable consumer recognition. 
ALSO READ: L&T bags large order worth ₹5,000 crore to deploy AI cluster in Chennai
 
Why Gold Spot disappeared
 
Gold Spot and Fanta occupied the same broad orange-flavoured carbonated drinks category. Coca-Cola eventually chose to concentrate its efforts behind Fanta, its established international brand, and phased out Gold Spot in 2000. A 2009 Business Today report noted that the company had struggled to manage overlapping brands after acquiring Parle's portfolio.
 
Other drinks such as Thums Up and Limca continued under Coca-Cola and retained distinct positions in the Indian market.
 
Why bring it back now?
 
The reported revival comes as India's carbonated drinks market becomes more competitive, with Reliance Consumer Products' Campa and regional challenger Lahori Zeera are gaining ground in a market traditionally dominated by Coca-Cola and PepsiCo.
 
According to a report in The Economic Times, the combined market share of smaller players, led by Campa and Lahori Zeera, nearly doubled to 15 per cent in January-September 2025, from around 7 per cent a year earlier. The combined share of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo fell to about 85 per cent from 93 per cent over the same period.
 
In April, Reliance said its beverages brand Campa has become the fourth-largest carbonated soft drinks player in India, with over ₹4,700 crore in gross sales in FY26 and a double-digit market share in key markets. ITC has also entered the segment with its sugar-free Coconut Cola, priced at ₹60 for a 250-ml can, targeting consumers willing to pay a premium for alternative formulations.
 
The other significant shift is towards beverages with lower sugar content. Sales of zero- and low-sugar drinks in India rose significantly, moving from about 5 per cent of the overall beverage market in 2020 to an average of roughly 30 per cent by 2025, and surging even higher through 2026, according to media reports.
 
Gold Spot, which Coca-Cola is reportedly bringing back in a low-sugar or no-sugar formulation, could therefore tap into a growing market for drinks that offer the taste of traditional soft drinks with less sugar.

data.title: Low P/E investing alone is a bad strategy: Harini Dedhia explains why
data.description:
Disclaimer: This article is written by Harini Dedhia, fund manager at Tamohara Investment Managers. Views expressed are her own. Readers' discretion is advised.
 Two recent moves in the market have everyone convinced of the ‘purist’ view of value investing. The first saw NIFTY IT move 17.5 per cent in the month of October alone; starting from a bottom valuation of 17.7 P/E (Price-to-Earnings Ratio) vs. the 10 year median of 25.1. The second saw NIFTY 50 move 16 per cent from the bottom it made on 8th October; from a 19 P/E vs. the 10 year median for the index at 23.2.
 
 
This has convinced many investors that buying companies within a certain P/E band alone is a good strategy. That has, however, not been the case in India, at least for the past 10 years. Almost the opposite has always been true. “Expensive” stocks are so because of the strength in underlying earnings growth and that momentum in earnings has sustained, securing returns for investors. 
 
Looking at the ten most expensive and cheap companies in NIFTY50 by trailing twelve months P/E Ratio reveals that the opposite has been true. Expensive companies on average (and median) have outperformed the benchmark by a margin.
 
For the past 10Y, NIFTY 50 has delivered a CAGR of 12.5 per cent. Only 2 of 10 companies from the ‘Cheap Ten’ have beaten that 10Y performance. For ‘Expensive Ten’ the number is 8 out 10.  
 
Favorable valuation ex of growth has no bearing on stock price performance. Both the companies from ‘Cheap Ten’ that have outperformed the index are ones that have outperformed on earnings too. Both Hindalco and SBI have respectively demonstrated a 10Y EPS CAGR of 76 per cent and 19 per cent. The 10Y average EPS growth is also solely skewed by this earnings performance by Hindalco. Ex of this, the average is much closer to the median EPS CAGR at 11 per cent.  
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 800 pts, Nifty below 25,600; Nifty Defence drops 1%
 
There is only one company in the ‘Cheap Ten’ bucket that has delivered 10Y EPS growth of over NIFTY 50’s EPS growth at 14.5 per cent (100bps over benchmark’s) but has still underperformed NIFTY50’s CAGR at 11.25 per cent (125bps under the benchmark CAGR). No points for guessing that this company is HDFC Bank and perhaps the hunting ground for structural investment ideas. 
 
It is not surprising that this relationship between earnings growth and stock price is seen in the underperformers from the ‘Expensive 10’ group as well. The two companies that have underperformed the index have done so on earnings growth as well- Asian Paints by 360bps at 9.9 per cent EPS CAGR and Hindustan Unilever by 60bps at 12.9 per cent EPS CAGR.  
One can attempt to discredit this assessment by stating that the current trailing twelve month P/E captures the up move these companies have seen and therefore is not the appropriate tool. Even if we recreate the ‘Expensive 10’ and ‘Cheap 10’ based on the historical 10Y average P/E, the answer does not change. The difference in performance remains stark.  
 
The same two companies are the underperformers from the ‘Expensive 10’ category on a 10Y basis. Perhaps the trap to avoid is higher P/E stocks with decelerating growth rather than higher P/E stocks altogether.

data.title: India's new GDP series brings demand, supply estimates closer: RBI DG Gupta
data.description:
The new gross domestic product (GDP) series has narrowed the gap between estimates derived from the demand and supply sides of the economy, addressing a key limitation of the earlier series, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said on Monday.
 
Under the previous series, the two estimates did not always align, with the resulting discrepancy at times being large and volatile. The revised series brings them together through a supply-use table framework, resulting in a much closer alignment of nominal GDP estimates.
 
“In the earlier series, GDP estimates from the demand and supply sides did not always align. The resulting gap was reported separately as a discrepancy, and it could at times be large and volatile,” Gupta said.
 
 
“The new series brings the two sides together through the supply-use table framework. As a result, nominal GDP estimates from both sides align much more closely. A small gap may still persist in real terms because the two sides are deflated differently, but it is much narrower than before,” she said.
 
The revised national accounts series, with 2022-23 as the base year, replacing 2011-12, incorporates a wider range of surveys and administrative data. It also uses double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture, in line with international best practices.
 
Gupta said the revision reflected the changes in the Indian economy over the past decade.
 
“The new series reflects an economy that has become larger, more diversified and more complex since the base was last revised in 2011-12,” she said.
 
On the demand side, private final consumption expenditure estimates now use shares from the more recent Household Consumption Expenditure Survey. Gross fixed capital formation has also been mapped to the sector investing in each asset, whether public, private, corporate or household.
 
“One can now assess not just how much is being invested, but also how much is being invested and in what,” Gupta said.
 
The changes are expected to improve the assessment of growth drivers and make early estimates more stable, with smaller revisions across successive data releases. “This has improved our ability to analyse, forecast and explain the drivers of economic growth from both the demand and supply sides,” she said.
 
Early GDP estimates, which rely on proxy indicators and provisional information, are an important input into monetary policy, Gupta said.
 
“The improvements in the new series are expected to make estimates more stable across successive vintages, with smaller revisions. This, in turn, will support better-calibrated and more stable policy, particularly monetary policy,” she said.
 
Gupta also highlighted the changes in the consumer price index (CPI), saying the revised series would better reflect evolving household consumption patterns and improve inflation measurement.
 
The new CPI series uses the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey of 2023-24 instead of the 2011-12 survey. It follows the United Nations’ Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018, allowing for a more detailed classification of consumption. The revised methodology includes better handling of missing data, particularly for seasonal items, and changes in the way household indices are combined. Housing is now covered in rural areas, while prices from 12 online markets are being collected for the first time.
 
“As the share of online consumption grows, this will matter for how we read price signals,” Gupta said.
 
The expanded coverage also includes item-level indices for rural, urban and combined sectors, as well as all states and Union Territories. This would help policymakers assess whether price pressures were concentrated in particular regions or were more widespread.
 
“These revisions should narrow the disconnect between measured and perceived inflation and add value to the conduct of monetary policy under our inflation-targeting framework,” she said.
 
Gupta said a base revision was not merely a technical exercise but an important tool for understanding structural changes in the economy.
 
“A base revision is not merely a routine technical update. It records important shifts in the structure of the economy, its evolving sectoral composition, changing household consumption behaviour, the segments that are growing rapidly, the organisation of economic activity and the sources of growth,” she said. “Better measurement of all these shifts is important for policymaking,” she added.
 
The revisions to GDP and CPI are expected to strengthen the RBI's assessment of economic conditions and improve the calibration of monetary policy, particularly by making early estimates more stable and inflation readings less volatile. Gupta said monetary policy decisions depended on an assessment of both current conditions and projections. Early estimates, which rely on proxy indicators and provisional information, were therefore an important input into the policy process.
 
The improved GDP series is expected to reduce the extent of revisions across successive estimates, allowing policymakers to work with a more stable assessment of growth. “The improvements in the new series are expected to make estimates more stable across successive vintages, with smaller revisions. This, in turn, will support better-calibrated and more stable policy, particularly monetary policy,” Gupta said.
 
The revised CPI, meanwhile, is expected to make headline inflation less volatile and the policy process less uncertain. The RBI uses inflation data alongside growth indicators to assess the evolving macroeconomic outlook.
 
Gupta said the changes in the CPI would help the central bank better understand price pressures across regions and consumption categories, while narrowing the gap between measured and perceived inflation. “These revisions should narrow the disconnect between measured and perceived inflation and add value to the conduct of monetary policy under our inflation-targeting framework,” she said.

data.title: From Bisleri to PepsiCo: FSSAI steps up action against food companies
data.description:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up action against food and beverage companies in recent months, targeting issues ranging from food safety violations to misleading product claims and labelling irregularities. Bisleri International is the latest to come under its scrutiny.
 
FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri after a sample of its packaged drinking water from its Goa facility was declared unsafe, with bromate levels exceeding the prescribed limit. A referral laboratory also detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
 
Bisleri has challenged the findings, saying independent tests found bromate levels within permissible limits. It said it submitted the results to FSSAI earlier this year in February and would continue to cooperate with the regulator.
  
Here are the recent actions taken by the regulator against food companies.

Nestle, Zydus face notices over product claims

In October, FSSAI issued notices to Nestle India and Zydus Wellness over alleged misleading claims on their products.
 
Nestle was asked to provide scientific evidence supporting claims on its Lactogen Pro 1 and Nan Excella Pro Stage 1 infant nutrition products. The regulator questioned claims relating to whey protein digestibility and immune system support.
 
Zydus Wellness received a notice over claims made for Complan, including its advertisements and product promotions. 
ALSO READ: FSSAI suspends licences of five nutraceutical firms over safety violations

PepsiCo, Red Bull face scrutiny over energy drink labels

FSSAI also initiated action against major energy drink manufacturers over the use of the 'energy drink' label.
 
In an affidavit before the Delhi High Court in November, the regulator accused PepsiCo of marketing its Sting and Adrenaline Rush beverages as energy drinks despite the absence of prescribed standards for the category.
 
FSSAI also raised concerns over similar labelling by Red Bull, Monster, Hell Energy and Reliance Consumer Products' Campa Energy Drink.
 
The regulator had earlier directed manufacturers to stop using the 'energy drink' descriptor. The companies challenged the directions in court.
 
FSSAI subsequently issued a fresh show-cause notice to Red Bull India, seeking scientific evidence to support its use of the label.

Six nutraceutical manufacturers face action

In November, FSSAI took regulatory action against six nutraceutical manufacturers over violations involving ingredients, product composition and manufacturing hygiene.
 
The companies were Airen Herbals, Aquabliss Lifesciences, Raskam Healthcare, Supercure Biotech, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare and Vedant Remedies.
 
The violations included the use of expired and non-permitted ingredients, excessive levels of certain nutrients, misleading product claims and poor manufacturing conditions. FSSAI also suspended licences in connection with some of the violations. 
ALSO READ: Bisleri challenges FSSAI's unsafe-sample finding, says water safe to drink

Priyagold maker, Dodla Dairy face prosecution

In October, FSSAI initiated prosecution against Surya Food and Agro, the maker of Priyagold biscuits, Dodla Dairy and Ueir Organic Foods over food safety violations.
 
The regulator found that bran meant for cattle feed had been used as an ingredient in Priyagold biscuits. A sample of Dodla Dairy's full-cream milk was found to be substandard, while samples of yellow raisins from Ueir Organic Foods contained pesticide residues above permissible limits.
 
FSSAI also issued notices to three other food businesses over safety and hygiene deficiencies.
 
FSSAI inspected 56,431 food establishments across the country between September 1 and November 5, collected 43,939 samples and found 2,273 of the 23,648 samples analysed to be non-compliant. The enforcement drive resulted in 410 prosecutions, 1,133 licence suspensions and the seizure of food products worth ₹81.8 crore.

data.title: BSE Realty index soars 17% in November; what's driving real estate stocks?
data.description:
BSE Realty index movement

 
Shares of real estate companies extended their rally, with the BSE Realty index hitting a 52-week high of 7,401.10, gaining 1 per cent on the BSE in Monday’s intraday deals on expectations of an improved demand outlook in the second half of the financial year 2026-27 (H1FY27). The realty index quoted at its highest level since November 6, 2025.
 
At 11:37 AM, the BSE Realty index was up 0.48 per cent at 7,355.19, while the Nifty Realty index was up 0.30 per cent. In comparison, the BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 indices were down 0.80 per cent each. The Nifty Realty index also hit a 52-week high of 947.70 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in intraday trade. 
 
 
Thus far in the month of November 2026, the BSE Realty index outperformed the market by soaring 16.6 per cent, compared to a 11.85 per cent rise in the BSE Sensex. Aditya Birla Real Estate, Lodha Developers, Prestige Estates Projects, Godrej Properties and Phoenix Mills rallied between 18-23 per cent in November.
 
Since April, the realty index zoomed 47 per cent. Share price of Sri Lotus Developers and Realty more than doubled or skyrocketed 129 per cent, while Lodha Developers and DLF surged 82 per cent and 58 per cent, respectively. Phoenix Mills, Godrej Properties, Prestige Estates Projects and Oberoi Realty soared in the range of 32-54 per cent during the period. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 

What’s driving real estate stocks?

 
Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said that its real estate coverage universe reported 26 per cent year-on-year (YoY) pre-sales growth in the July to September 2026 quarter (Q2FY27), led by a 7x jump for Oberoi Realty with its stellar foray in NCR. Excluding Oberoi Realty, MOFSL’s coverage posted 3 per cent YoY growth, which was on expected lines, despite no major launches. 
 
“For our coverage, 2QFY27 pre-sales at ₹42,800 crore were the third highest quarterly performance in any year despite Q2 being seasonally weak. This was broadly driven by strong sustenance sales, which highlights the underlying demand strength,” analysts at MOFSL said.
 
Balance sheet of the sector remains healthy, with net debt (ex-Lotus Developers) declining by ₹1,400 crore quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) (down by 76 per cent after FY17). Companies have broadly maintained their FY27 guidance, and analysts at MOFSL expect DLF, Prestige Estates Projects, Oberoi Realty, Brigade Enterprises and Lodha Developers to outperform peers in H2FY27. Valuations are comfortable, with larger developers trading closer to net asset value (NAV) and most small-medium companies trading at 20-65 per cent discount to the residential NAV, the brokerage firm said.
 
Meanwhile, analysts at Axis Securities remain constructive on the Real Estate sector, with H2FY27 expected to benefit from an expanded project launch pipeline and continued geographical diversification. The strong response to Oberoi Realty's first NCR project, alongside healthy demand across Prestige's Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai markets, reinforces the resilience of premium housing demand. 
 
Developers continue to maintain disciplined balance sheets while actively pursuing land acquisitions, joint development agreements and new project opportunities. Rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, and premiumisation are expected to sustain housing demand. The brokerage firm believes the next phase of sector growth will be driven primarily by new launches, project execution and geographical expansion rather than aggressive price appreciation.
 
Analysts at PL Capital maintain a constructive stance on developers with strong launch pipelines, balance sheet discipline, and execution track record. Preference remains for players with Bengaluru/Mumbai exposure, premium positioning, and near-term launch visibility, which are best placed to sustain pre-sales growth into FY27E. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Cons durables, autos: Systematix bullish on 2 sectors amid metal price fall
data.description:
The sharp correction in global metal prices could offer a margin boost to Indian consumer durable and automobile companies, even as it raises earnings risks for metal producers, particularly non-ferrous players, according to a report by Systematix Institutional Equities. 
 
Copper, zinc and steel prices have fallen 16 per cent, 21 per cent and 5 per cent, respectively, creating scope for lower input costs and improved profitability across downstream sectors. Systematix is most positive on consumer durables, followed by automobiles, while remaining cautious on metals, with consumer durable companies seen as the biggest beneficiaries of the commodity price correction.
 
The brokerage noted that Copper and zinc prices have come under pressure due to a combination of macroeconomic factors, weakening industrial demand, rising inventories and profit booking after a strong rally since mid-2025. A stronger US dollar, expectations of higher US interest rates and continued weakness in Chinese construction and manufacturing activity have further weighed on sentiment
 
 
Meanwhile, China's October industrial production growth undershot market expectations, while fixed asset investment remained weak. Crude steel production declined 1.6 per cent y-o-y, pointing to softer industrial activity and lower demand for industrial metals. The slowdown is particularly negative for zinc, given its extensive use in galvanised steel production.
 
Notably, Copper sentiment has also weakened amid concerns that expectations of AI-led demand growth may have become overly optimistic. According to S&P Global, data centres currently account for only about 4 per cent of global copper demand, limiting the magnitude of any AI-related demand uplift, the brokerage said.
 
In the auto sector, the brokerage noted that two-wheelers are likely to be the biggest beneficiaries due to their relatively higher exposure to aluminium and copper. Combined with stable pricing and operating leverage benefits, earnings momentum could strengthen over the coming quarters. Systematix preferred picks include Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor, Eicher Motors, Hyundai Motor India, Tata Motors (CV).
 
In the consumer durables sector, Systematix’s analysis suggests that consumer durables exhibit the highest earnings sensitivity to lower metal prices. In addition, the sector continues to trade at a more than 40 per cent discount to its five-year average relative valuation, creating an attractive riskreward proposition if commodity prices remain subdued. The brokerage’s preferred picks remain Voltas, Blue Star, Havells India, and Crompton Greaves Consumer.
 
Meanwhile, in the metal space, the brokerage noted that after a prolonged period of outperformance, earnings expectations for metal companies appear vulnerable to a combination of weaker commodity prices, slowing global industrial activity and rising inventories. The risks are particularly pronounced for non-ferrous producers where earnings remain highly sensitive to copper and zinc prices. The stocks that remain at risk include Hindustan Zinc, Hindustan Copper, Vedanta.
